gates.claim: Frozen q=2 binary-route train/held-out dimensional, topology-precursor and observer-smoothing controls pass in the declared finite protocol.
The selected q=2 cross-polytope PL completion is a recursive orientable 3-manifold completion with the declared link and homology checks; dynamical uniqueness is not claimed.

On the selected 16-cell PL completion, the four q=2 face carriers admit an exact globally consistent face colouring: the dual graph is Q4, shared faces carry the same label, neighboring cell orientations alternate and outward Walsh fluxes cancel pairwise.

Four active q=2 states alone cannot carry the Peter-Weyl (2,2) link, but adjoining the graph-changing no-link/j=0 singlet gives the exact SO(5) vector decomposition (2,2)+(1,1); its transporter toggles active and no-link sectors and factors the frozen q=2 Hamming adjacency exactly through two graph-changing steps.

If n indistinguishable active q=2 graph-link strands are symmetrically blocked at both endpoints, the coarse link is the unique (j,j)=(n/2,n/2) sector of dimension (n+1)^2, and occupancy n=0..N reproduces the Peter-Weyl tower through Jmax=N/2 exactly in representation content and dimension.

Finite Peter-Weyl SU(2) geometry, Euclidean Hamiltonian, volume/extrinsic-curvature and covariant composition gates pass within the declared cutoff domains.
Independent dual-cell sharp, path-diffeomorphism and route-normal HDA principal-symbol gates pass on the declared finite probes.

A frozen three-node Euclidean Peter-Weyl by route off-shell regression retains j=0 cylindrical graph-change outputs and reproduces route~epsilon, cross~epsilon, pure-geometry~epsilon^2 and joint~epsilon scaling across all three node-pair commutators.
The fixed real-beta Lorentzian coefficient control and finite Peter-Weyl support bound pass through the declared regulator-safe cutoff window.

For the explicitly stated fixed-cutoff habitat assumptions, the composition algebra gives cross/D = O(epsilon) and geometry-geometry/D = O(epsilon^2), reducing the full defect to the route defect in the epsilon-to-zero limit.

For the frozen all-j=1/2 finite-HH family, the exact hit-depth support theorem makes Peter-Weyl truncation identically zero above Jmax=5/2 in the Euclidean three-node calculation, while the measured joint HDA defect decreases as epsilon^1.00644; the conservative Lorentzian support wall is Jmax=13/2.
Within the declared local two-derivative canonical ansatz, the documented HDA/DeWitt signature and degree-counting results identify the GR kinetic structure required by first-class closure.

The three-node graph-changing finite hierarchy passes, but arbitrary-graph, Lorentzian, multi-habitat off-shell quantum HDA closure with an independently fixed structure-function target is not yet proved.
The fixed-input simultaneous epsilon/Peter-Weyl limit is controlled, but a uniform regulator/refinement theorem for growing graph size and collective input spin remains open.

The q=2 labels now generate/glue a tetrahedral carrier; active q=2 labels plus the existing no-link state give an exact j=1/2 graph-link representation and conditional symmetric blocking supplies the Peter-Weyl tower. Still open are dynamical selection of the SO(5) transporter/coarse symmetric sector, occupancy weights and the semiclassical geometric measure from generic microscopic states.

A preregistered blind prediction of an external physical observable, including a common physical scale map and uncertainty accounting, remains open; selection-tainted dimension/z targets and oracle S4 Lambda are explicitly excluded.

The registered finite/exact mathematical bridge is internally composable when the geometry, route-HDA and cutoff-support gates are combined; this is not arbitrary-graph quantum-GR closure or experimental confirmation.
